RENDER PROFILING

1. In Setup, enable diagnostics and logging, then enable render profiling.
   Choose 30-300 seconds; the default is 120. Launch with normal rendering settings.
2. Load a track and drive normally. Keep LMU focused on the desktop and press
   Ctrl+Alt+F9 once. A held key does not repeatedly toggle capture.
3. Capture ends at the duration boundary. The same shortcut ends it early.
   Deadlines and periodic checkpoints continue when XR menu frames are rendered.
4. Exit normally. Any active capture is saved on session/instance teardown and
   its log is flushed, including when teardown runs on another thread.
5. The package's logs/ directory contains quad-*.log and matching *-run.json.
   A completed or partial capture includes render_profile summary and complete.
   render_profile armed alone means no capture has been triggered.

CPU SLOTS

outer0/1          Original LMU eye render, including native resource-bank handling.
focus_hook0/1     Complete additional focus path after the original eye render.
focus_scene0/1    Native SceneRender invoked for the focus view.
focus_prepare0/1  Focus camera/history/projection preparation.
focus_restore0/1  Focus completion and restoration of outer camera state.
outer_copy0/1     Outer image validation, acquisition/wait and transfer.
outer_wait0/1     Acquisition/wait subset of outer_copy.
native_prepare0/1 Smaller native resource-bank validation and binding setup.
native_restore0/1 Native bindings/view/viewport restoration.
sort_outer0/1, sort_focus0/1
                 World render-group hooks where available for the active path.
ui               UI hook, including extra outer-view UI work.
provider_submit  Downstream xrEndFrame, including provider/runtime waits.
frame_interval   Time between consecutive scene frames, including frame pacing.
non_scene_ui, non_scene_provider_submit, non_scene_outer_wait0/1
                 Corresponding calls in XR frames without a verified scene.

Calls are accumulated per XR frame before computing mean, p50, p95, p99 and max.
Samples count frames with that scope; calls count invocations. The summary also
counts scene frames, completed XR frames and non-scene frames. Menu gaps are not
included in scene cadence, and tokens crossing abandoned frames are discarded.
Only the verified render thread records measurements. Missing slots mean no
samples were observed, not zero cost. Up to 65,536 frames are retained per slot;
overflow is counted as dropped.

CPU values are ELAPSED WALL TIME, including driver/runtime waits. Nested scopes
overlap: focus_hook includes focus_scene and preparation/restoration; sort
scopes are within render scopes. Do not sum parents and children or equate these
measurements to CPU utilization. No single-pass stereo or draw reduction occurs.

GPU SLOTS

outer0/1 and focus0/1 measure original outer and repeated focus rendering.
Queries are sampled across the full capture, targeting about 480 results per
slot, with a 512-sample limit. At 120 seconds the interval is about 250 ms.
DONOTFLUSH polling reads results asynchronously without explicit GPU Flush or
blocking query waits. Disjoint, failed, dropped and pending results are counted.
These slots omit copies, UI, provider composition and runtime encoding; they
cannot be treated as total GPU frame time.

OVERHEAD AND SAVING

Active diagnostics add clock reads, short locks, sample writes and sparse GPU
queries. Summary sorting/logging can hitch at the capture boundary. Use the same
profiling configuration for comparisons and disable diagnostics for normal play.
No particular CPU overhead or performance improvement is claimed.

CPU mean checkpoints are written every 15 seconds during capture. A normal close
saves partial statistics and flushes the log. Another teardown thread saves
completed GPU results without touching the D3D11 context; outstanding scopes and
queries are explicitly omitted. A killed/crashed process may retain checkpoints
but lose final percentiles and recent samples. No shutdown handler can guarantee
final saving after forced termination.

Untick Setup -> Enable diagnostics and logging, then relaunch to disable mod
logging, run metadata, profiling clocks/queries, legacy timing/benchmark triggers,
pixel statistics and view captures. This overrides saved profiling-on. Existing
logs remain, and the preference is saved. With diagnostics off there is no
capture to save at exit. Small disabled-feature checks remain. Provider/runtime
logs and overlays are controlled separately. The CLI equivalent is
mod/launch.ps1 -DisableDiagnostics; native enforcement is LMU_QV_DIAGNOSTICS=0.

Captures can contain personal installation paths and run details. Keep them out
of source commits. Compare the same track, car, grid and actual image sizes when
evaluating providers; slider labels can map to different dimensions.
